blocks.content: A tag is a human-readable label pointing at a specific image, it is not the image data itself. Understanding that distinction clears up a lot of confusion about how docker tag and versioning actually work.
1. A Tag Is Just a Pointer
blocks.text: 1. A Tag Is Just a Pointer

blocks.content: Internally, every image is identified by its content hash (the image ID). A tag like myapp:1.0 is simply a friendly name that points at one specific image ID, the same way a bookmark points at a page without being the page itself.

blocks.alt: The tag is a label, the image ID is what it actually points at

blocks.content: Because a tag is just a pointer, nothing stops multiple tags from pointing at the exact same underlying image. It is completely normal for myapp:1.2 and myapp:latest to reference identical image data, right up until the next build moves latest forward.

blocks.alt: Different labels, same underlying image data

blocks.content: Running docker tag creates a new pointer, it does not copy any image content. Retagging an image a dozen different ways costs essentially no extra disk space, since every tag still references the same shared layers.

blocks.alt: New pointer, zero new data on disk

blocks.content:
docker tag myapp:1.0 myapp:stable
docker tag myapp:1.0 myregistry.com/team/myapp:1.0
# Both new tags point at the exact same image ID as myapp:1.0

code.content:
docker tag myapp:1.0 myapp:stable
docker tag myapp:1.0 myregistry.com/team/myapp:1.0
# Both new tags point at the exact same image ID as myapp:1.0

codes.bash:
docker tag myapp:1.0 myapp:stable
docker tag myapp:1.0 myregistry.com/team/myapp:1.0
# Both new tags point at the exact same image ID as myapp:1.0

blocks.content: Relying on latest alone in production is a common mistake, it gives you no way to know exactly what is deployed. A more reliable strategy tags every build with something specific, a semantic version, or the git commit hash it was built from, and updates a floating tag like latest as a convenience on top of that.

blocks.alt: Specific, traceable tags alongside a convenience tag

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A tag is a pointer to an image ID, not the image itself, which is why multiple tags can reference identical data at zero extra cost.
Production deployments should be pinned to a specific, traceable tag (a version or a commit sha), not a floating one like latest.
